newsitem.title: USA: 1st gas price drop seen in N.Calif since Dec - CSAA.
newsitem.headline: 1st gas price drop seen in N.Calif since Dec - CSAA.

text.p: Retail gas prices in northern California fell for the first time in four months, as higher gasoline production eased supply concerns, the California State Automobile Association (CSAA) said Wednesday.
"The abundance of gasoline production in California is fulfilling the current demand and therefore mitigating prices throughout the state," said CSAA spokesman Ron Kennedy.
Self-serve unleaded gasoline now averages $1.43 a gallon in northern California, down three cents from CSAA's April 21 Fuel Gauge Survey.
The average for self-serve unleaded has dropped three to eight cents in northern California.
In the state capital, Sacramento, average prices have fallen five cents to $1.39 and $1.38.
San Francisco and Oakland's averages dropped three cents to $1.49 and $1.43 a gallon.
The regional averages for self-serve unleaded in northern California are 11 to 16 cents lower this May, compared to last year at this time.
The national average for self-serve unleaded gasoline is $1.24, down one cent from last month and six cents lower than a year ago.
